texts.preamble: Lakshminarayanaswamy vs Dhanalakshmi on 2 May, 2025 1 Crl.A.No.1075/2023 Judgment Kabc010209222023 In The Court Of The Lix Addl. City Civil & Sessions Judge, Bangalore City (Cch-60) Dated this the 2nd day of May 2025. Present: Sri Somashekara. A., B.A.L., Ll.M., Lix Addl. City Civil & Sessions Judge, Bangalore City . Crl. Appeal No.1075/2023
texts.facts: The appellant is respondent and the respondent is petitioner before the Trial Court. The petitioner has filed petition under section 12(1) of The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005, against the respondent seeking various reliefs under section 12, 18, 19, 22 and 23 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act for grant of interim reliefs. 4. According to the petitioner her marriage was solemnized with respondent on 27.04.1977 as per Hindu Rights and Customs at Tirumala Temple, Tirumala of Andra Pradesh and after the marriage she joined her matrimonial home at Parvathipuram Bengaluru. Out of their wedlock they be gotten 4 children. The respondent was working in Postal Department and she left the job in the year 1992 and indugled and political activities he started harassing the petitioner for want of funds. The petitioner was doing business of fair price depot, but in the year Judge sign Crl.A.No.1075/2023 Judgment 2005 without knowledge of the petitioner the respondent transfer the said shop into his name. 5. It is alleged that, since from the date of marriage the respondent harass the petitioner both physically and mentally. The petitioner has perform the marriage of all the children. Such being the case in the year 2005 the respondent sold immovable property situated at Chikkamavalli. The respondent assaulted the petitioner and thrown out of the house and claiming that the petitioner is not his legally wedded wife. Therefore, the present petition has been filed through the restraining the respondent from committing any Domestic Violence and also to restrain the respondent from dis-possessing the petitioner from her residence and not alienate the said property. 6. On receipt of notice the respondent appeared and contested the petitioner by filing his statement by denying the entire case of the complainant/petitioner. According to the respondent the complainant was member of association named Parvathipuram Ration Card Holder Society. The respondent was president of the said society. The complainant who was having children was deserted by her husband, as she was not having any mense of income. Complainant was in need of money, she appointed a secretary of said society. The complainant and respondent have never lived together. Such being the case at one point of time the complainant has stolen the Jewels house hold articles of the respondents on 30.01.1995 and escaped by abandoning her children by which the respondent has filed complaint before Kalasipalya Police Station. In view of the said complaint the complainant was irregulars and failed the attends the meeting of the society and do to which she was unanimously removed from the society and that grudge she has committed theft in fair prize depot and in that regard the and complaint was filed before Central police on 20.09.1995. In pursuance of that the complainant was in financial crises and she was always pestering the respondent for money Lakshminarayanaswamy vs Dhanalakshmi on 2 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112373537/ 2 and there by started blackmail the respondent in one or other way with an intention to extract the money and in the Judge sign Crl.A.No.1075/2023 Judgment process on 01.05.2006 she took Rs.2,00,000/- from the respondent and undertaken that she will not interfere with the respondent. With all these on 15.09.2016 on Palaksha son the petitioner has illegally breaking open the lock of the house of the respondent, trespassed and occupy the house of the respondent and in this connection he has lodged complaint before the Channamamakere Achukattu in Cr. No.234/2016, after noticing the said case, complainant and her friend Bhagya made quarrel with the complainant and in that regard the police have registered NCR NO. 165/2016 against the complainant. 7. The respondent specifically contended that the petitioner is not his wife, basically she was marriage to one Devaraj and thereafter she had affairs with one Shamiulla Sharif, such being the case in order to grab the house property of the respondent, the petitioner has got filed suit for partition through her son Palaksha against respondent in OS No. 7825/2016. Under these fact and circumstances, the present complaint filed by the petitioner/complainant against the respondent is not Judge sign Crl.A.No.1075/2023 Judgment maintainable. Amongst other ground he prayed to reject the complaint. 8. On the basis of rival contention of the parties the Trial Court recorded the evidence of both petitioner and respondent. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioner she herself examined as PW1 on 04.01.2018 and thereafter on 01.03.2018 she got produced documents at Ex.P1 to P4. After thorough rough cross examination conducted by the learned counsel for the respondent and wherein he has disputed the entire case of the petitioner. After taking such defense and lapse of five years i.e., on 30.01.2023 the complainant/ petitioner got produced 19 documents as per Ex.P5 to 19. All the documents have been seriously disputed by the respondent. 9. Aggrieved by the said order the present appeal has been field by the appellant. In the appeal memo it is contended that the Trial Court committed serious error in allowing the petition against the respondent. Further it is contended that the Trial Court Mechanically passed an order dated.05.07.2023. The serious contention taken by the respondent in respect of Ex.P.3, 7 to 15 have not been considered and appreciated in a prospective manner. Further the Trial Court fail to consider Ex.R.1/Consent letter executed by the petitioner/respondent. Therefore, the appellant submitted that the said order passed by the Trial Court is liable to the [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 4 they amicably settled that compromise and on 01.05.2006 the respondent Judge sign Crl.A.No.1075/2023 Judgment undertaken that she will not interfere with the life of the appellant.
texts.arguments: 12. The appellant has produced the reported Judgment in the case of Poonam Vs. V.P.Sharma in Crl.M.C.No.1105/2009 reported in 2014 (4) Crimes (SC) 374 and another case between Gaurav Mehta Vs. Anamika Chopra, decided in Crl.R.P.No.4152/2023 and Crl.R.P.No.4452/2023 by the Hon'ble High Court of Judicature at Allahabad. 14. My findings on the aforesaid points as follows:- Point No.1: In the Negative, Point No.2: In the Affirmative, Point No.3: As per final order, for the following:- REASONS 15. POINTS NO.1 & 2:- These points are interrelated, hence they are taken together for common discussion in order to avoid repetition of facts and evidence. The learned counsel for the appellant vehemently contended that the respondent is not the legally wedded wife of the appellant and their marriage was not solemnized at all and Judge sign Crl.A.No.1075/2023 Judgment petitioner is not begatton any children to the respondent. In fact the respondent was married to one Devaraj and out of their wedlock children were born the said respondent deserted her husband Devaraj on the ground that she had affair with one Shamiulla Shariff. Ex. R.13 to Ex.P.15/Birth Certificates clearly discloses that the respondent Smt.Dhanalakshmi is a wife of one Devaraj and Shamiulla Shariff. Therefore, the appellant strongly contended that the respondent is not his legally wedded wife. Further the learned counsel for appellant argued that the respondent was appointed has a Secretary in Parvathipura Ration Card holder society, wherein she had come in contact with the appellant and in the year 1995 she stolen jewels and household articles of the appellant and as such complaint was lodged on 30.01.1995 and 20.09.1995 respectively, out of that venjens the respondent started blackmail to the appellant and Lakshminarayanaswamy vs Dhanalakshmi on 2 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112373537/ Such being the case the question of alleging the Domestic Violence against the appellant does not arise. To counter this argument the respondent counsel has not submitted anything, he has stated that arguments may be taken as heard. 18. The second contention urged by the counsel for the appellant is that as per Ex.R.1 consent letter dated.01.05.2006 clearly discloses that the respondent petitioner has received an amount of Rs.2,00,000/- Permanent Alimony towards maintenance amount and she undertaken that she will not claim Judge sign Crl.A.No.1075/2023 Judgment any amount of money from the appellant. On the basis of the said document the learned counsel for the appellant much argued that the petition filed by the respondent before the Trial Court under section 12 of DV Act is not maintainable. As per section 2(A) of D.V. Act aggrieved person means any women who is, are has been in a Domestic Violence with the respondent who alleged to have subjected to any act of Domestic Violence by the respondent. Section 2(a) of the Act reads as under: "(a) "aggrieved person" means any woman who is, or has been in domestic relationship with the respondent and who alleges to have been subjected to any act of domestic violence by the respondent" The "domestic relationship" has been defined in section 2(f) of the said Domestic Violence Act which reads as under:- "(f) "domestic relationship" means a relationship between two persons who live or have, at any point of time, lived together in a shared household when they are related by consanguinity, marriage, or through a Judge sign Crl.A.No.1075/2023 Judgment relationship in the nature of marriage, adoption or are family members living together as joint family" The Word "respondent" has been defined under section 2Q of the said Act which reads thus: "(a) "respondent" means any adult male person who is, or has been, in a domestic relationship with the aggrieved person and against whom the aggrieved person has sought any relief under this Act." 24. As such petitioner was under an obligation to prove that she had been living together with the respondent in relationship which was in the nature of marriage. While dealing with the similar issue in the case of D. Velusamy Versus D. Patchaiammall, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed as under: "31. In our opinion a 'relationship in the nature of marriage' is akin to a common law marriage. Common law marriages require that although not being formally married. Judge sign Crl.A.No.1075/2023 Judgment (a) The couple must hold themselves out to society as being akin to spouses. (b) They must be of legal age to marry. Lakshminarayanaswamy vs Dhanalakshmi on 2 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112373537/ 7 (c) They must be otherwise qualified to enter into a legal marriage, including being unmarried. (d) They must have voluntarily cohabited and held themselves out to the world as being akin to spouses for a significant period of time. (see 'Common Law Marriage' in Wikipedia on Google) If a man has a 'keep' whom he maintains financially and uses mainly for sexual purpose and/or as a servant it would not, in our opinion, be a relationship in the nature of marriage' 26. 27. Similar issue was raised before the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Indra Sarma Vs. V.K.V. Sarma. Dealing with the live in relationship, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the said judgment at paragraph Nos. 61, 62, 63 and 66 had observed as under " 61. Such relationship, it may be noted, may endure for a Judge sign Crl.A.No.1075/2023 Judgment long time and can result pattern of dependency and vulnerability, and increasing number of such relationships, calls for adequate and effective protection, especially to the woman and children born out of that live-in- relationship. Legislature, of course, cannot promote pre-marital sex, though, at times, such relationships are intensively personal and people may express their opinion, for and against. See S Khushboo v. Kanniammal and another (2010) 5 SCC 600. 28. Parliament has to ponder over these issues, bring in proper legislation or make a proper amendment of the Act, so that women and the children, born out of such kinds of relationships be protected, though those types of relationship might not be a relationship in the nature of a marriage. 31. The next bone of contention urged by the learned counsel for the respondent is that essential ceremonies of Hindu Marriage had not been performed, The decision rendered by a Single Judge of the Court in (Samarapu Satyanarayana v. Vijaya Laxmi) is to the effect that in the absence of domestic relationship between the petitioner and respondent, respondent will not be recognized as an aggrieved person as defined under section 2(a) of the Act, In the present case disputed question of fact are occurring that can be resolved Judge sign Crl.A.No.1075/2023 Judgment only when the evidence that would be let in by the respective parties in DVC, but in this case the petitioner has failed to establish that she was in domestic relationship with the respondent.
